title: Optimization II
subtitle: Finish the job: the derivative, the critical number, the check, and the answer to the question asked.

questions.text: After finding a critical point, you should check that it really gives a max (or min).
questions.explain: Use the first or second derivative test, or compare with the endpoints. Skipping this loses points on the exam.

questions.text: Put the optimization steps in order.
items: Draw a diagram and name the variables
Decide what to optimize (max or min)
Use the constraint to get one variable
Check it is really a max or min, then answer the question
questions.explain: The steps from the class slides.

questions.text: A continuous function on a closed interval $[a, b]$ has its absolute maximum…
options: at a critical number or at an endpoint
questions.hint: This is the closed interval method.
questions.explain: Compare the values at the critical numbers and at both endpoints. The largest one wins.

questions.text: A problem asks for the **dimensions** of the largest pen, and you find $x$ = 300. Are you done?
options: No. Find $y$ too, and answer the question that was asked
questions.hint: Read the last sentence of the problem again.
questions.explain: Dimensions means both sides. Always go back and answer what was asked.

questions.text: If the function has only one critical number in its interval and $f''$ is negative there, that critical number gives the absolute maximum.
questions.hint: One hilltop and no valleys.
questions.explain: With a single critical number, a local max there is the absolute max.

questions.text: In the fence problem, $x$ has to be between 0 and 600. Where do those limits come from?
questions.hint: What must be true of the two sides of a real pen?
questions.explain: Both sides have to be at least 0. That gives the interval to search.
